headline: High data-leakage and cascading-error risk: Chatwoot’s broad egress can expose customer data while LlamaFactory has no filesystem/network access to contain or verify it.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented. Chatwoot has broad network egress, but LlamaFactory has no stdin/stdout, clipboard, filesystem, MCP, or browser surfaces, so there is no plausible default path for Chatwoot content to inject instructions into LlamaFactory.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator copies Chatwoot output into LlamaFactory prompts, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between the agents, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the agents disconnected from shared queues and copy-paste bridges.
Disable any future prompt relay between Chatwoot and LlamaFactory.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a bridge is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, and messages, and it has broad network egress. LlamaFactory is local-only with no network egress and no file access, so direct leakage from B is blocked, but Chatwoot can still send sensitive data to external APIs in default integrations.
conditions: IF Chatwoot integrations forward customer messages or orders to third-party services, leakage occurs.
IF LlamaFactory is later given file or network access, the leakage surface expands.
mitigations: Audit enabled Chatwoot integrations and disable unused ones.
Restrict Chatwoot egress with an allowlist.
Redact customer identifiers before outbound API calls.
requires-engineering: add DLP controls on Chatwoot outbound payloads.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Chatwoot has broad network egress, but LlamaFactory has no filesystem write, no git modification, no shell, and no network egress. With no overlapping mutable resource, there is no default write-write conflict between the pair.
conditions: IF LlamaFactory is reconfigured with write access to the same workspace as Chatwoot, conflict risk appears.
IF both agents are granted shared OAuth scopes or shared mutable storage, the assessment changes.
mitigations: Separate Chatwoot and any training workspace directories.
Avoid shared credentials between the agents.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Chatwoot can emit support content and reports, and LlamaFactory is an LLM training/fine-tuning tool that could consume such outputs if an operator feeds them in. There is no documented verification or coordination layer, so the pair can propagate unverified Chatwoot outputs into downstream model work.
conditions: IF Chatwoot outputs are used as training or evaluation data for LlamaFactory without review, errors cascade.
IF an operator manually curates and verifies the data first, the risk drops.
mitigations: Require human review before exporting Chatwoot outputs.
Sample-check labels and transcripts before training.
Keep a signed provenance log for imported datasets.
requires-engineering: add validation gates before LlamaFactory ingestion.

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot clearly handles customer data and messages, while LlamaFactory’s profile shows no data classes touched and no residency or retention controls. If customer data is moved from Chatwoot into LlamaFactory workflows, the mismatch in documented handling and retention creates a compliance gap, though not enough evidence for a higher severity.
conditions: IF customer messages or orders are exported from Chatwoot into LlamaFactory training data, compliance review is required.
IF retention or deletion requests must propagate across both systems, the gap becomes operational.
mitigations: Do not export regulated customer data into LlamaFactory by default.
Document retention and deletion handling for any shared dataset.
requires-engineering: align data-processing terms and residency controls.
